How could Wáng and Shěn go out to Běidì?
This mention of Běidì
refers to the lands north of Cháng'ān.
Jǐ,
jū qǐ fān.
"Zhèn'è wants to kill all the southerners,
sending a few dozen men to escort Yìzhēn back south,
and thereby seize Guānzhōng and rebel."
Xīnhài,
Tiánzǐ invited Zhèn'è to Fù Hóngzhī's camp to discuss matters.
Tiánzǐ requested to dismiss others for a private talk,
and had his clansman Shěn Jìngrén behead him beneath the tent,
falsely claiming he had received the Grand Commandant's order to execute him.
Hóngzhī rushed to report to Liú Yìzhēn.
Yìzhēn and Wáng Xiū donned armor and ascended the Héng Gate to observe the situation.
Héng Gate,
the first gate on the eastern end of the northern wall of Cháng'ān city.
Bèi,
pí yì fān.
Héng,
yīn guāng.
He said Zhèn'è had rebelled.
Xiū arrested Tiánzǐ,
enumerated his crime of unauthorized killing,
and executed him.
He appointed Champion General Máo Xiūzhī to replace Zhèn'è as Chief Clerk to the Pacification of the West.
Fù Hóngzhī greatly defeated Hèlián Guī at Chíyáng,
and again defeated him at Guǎfù Dù.
According to Sòng Bái's *Xù Tōngdiǎn*,
fifteen *lǐ* north of present-day Qìngzhōu is Guǎfù Mountain.
It seems a river originates from this mountain,
and its lower reaches form Guǎfù Dù.
The Xià troops then withdrew.
Rénxū,
Grand Commandant Yù arrived at Péngchéng,
and lifted the state of alert.
Prince of Lángyá Sīmǎ Déwén had first returned to Jiànkāng.
Yù heard of Wáng Zhèn'è's death,
and submitted a memorial stating
"Shěn Tiánzǐ suddenly became violently deranged,
and treacherously harmed a loyal and meritorious official."
Kuáng yì,
means becoming mad and changing one's normal mind.
Yì,
rú zì.
He appointed Péngchéng Neishi Liú Zūnkǎo as Governor of Bìngzhōu and concurrently Administrator of Hédōng,
garrisoning Púbǎn.
He summoned Governor of Jīngzhōu Liú Dàolián to be Governor of Xú and Yǎn Provinces.
Yù wished to have his heir apparent Yìfú garrison Jīngzhōu,
and have Governor of Xúzhōu Liú Yìlóng be Governor of Sīzhōu,
garrisoning Luòyáng.
Central Army Consultant Zhāng Shào remonstrated:
Consultant,
means Consultant to the Army.
"The importance of the heir apparent
concerns the whole realm.
He should not be stationed outside."
So instead, he made Yìlóng Commander of Military Affairs of the Six Provinces of Jīng, Yì, Níng, Yōng, Liáng, and Qín, Western Central General, and Governor of Jīngzhōu.
He appointed Administrator of Nánjùn Dào Yànzhī as Colonel of the Southern Man,
Zhāng Shào as Chief Clerk and concurrently Chancellor of Nánjùn,
Champion Merit Official Wáng Tánshǒu as Chief Clerk,
and Běixúzhōu Attendant Wáng Huá as Registrar to the Western Central General.
Jìn established Southern Xúzhōu at Jīngkǒu,
while Northern Xúzhōu remained administered from Péngchéng.
Dào Yànzhī, Wáng Tánshǒu, and Wáng Huá assisted Yìlóng in his establishment and entry,
and subsequently held the positions of generals and ministers.
Yìlóng was still young,
and all matters of his administration were decided by Shào.
Tánshǒu
was Hóngzhī's younger brother.
Yù said to Yìlóng:
"Wáng Tánshǒu is composed, resolute, and possesses capacity and bearing.
He is ministerial material.
You should consult him on every matter."
He appointed Duke of Nánjùn Liú Yìqìng as Governor of Yùzhōu.
Yìqìng
was Dàolián's son.
Yù relinquished Sīzhōu,
and took on the governorships of Xú and Jì Provinces.
4. Qín King Chìpán appointed Qǐfú Mùyìgān as Governor of Shāzhōu,
garrisoning Lèdū.
5. Second month,
Bǐfú Wūdìyán led twenty thousand households and surrendered to Qín.
6. Third month,
they sent an envoy to Wèi to establish relations.
7. Summer,
fourth month,
Jǐsì,
Wèi relocated the Túhé people from Jì, Dìng, and Yōu Provinces to the Dàidū region.
Wèi sovereign Guī, in the second year of Huángshǐ, captured Zhōngshān,
established Ānzhōu,
and also set up a branch secretariat to pacify and govern its people.
In the third year of Tiānxīng,
it was renamed Dìngzhōu,
overseeing Zhōngshān, Chángshān, Jùlù, Bólíng, Běipíng, Héjiān, Gāoyáng, and Zhàojùn.
Sòng Bái said: Initially Ānzhōu was established,
soon renamed Dìngzhōu,
named for pacifying and stabilizing the realm.
Túhé,
likely refers to the Túhé people who followed the Mùróng into the Central Plains and remained settled in the three provinces. The Wèi people thus called them Túhé.
In the eleventh month,
Língshí arrived at Cháng'ān.
Yìzhēn's officers and soldiers were greedy and unrestrained,
plundering extensively as they headed east,
carrying large amounts of treasure, goods, women, and children,
moving slowly in double columns.
Wéi Huá, the Assistant Inspector of Yōng Province, fled to Xià.
Wéi Huá was originally a subject of the Yáo clan,
and Yù appointed him as Assistant Inspector of Yōng Province.
General Fù Hóngzhī of the Jianwei Army said:
"The Duke ordered us to advance quickly;
now with so much baggage and supplies,
we cannot travel more than ten li in a day.
If the enemy's pursuing cavalry catches up,
how will we deal with them!
We should abandon the carts and travel light,
only then can we escape."
Yìzhēn did not listen.
Soon after, a large force of Xià troops arrived,
Fù Hóngzhī and Kuǎi Ān covered the rear,
fighting fiercely for several days.
When they reached Qīngní,
the Jìn troops were utterly defeated,
Hóngzhī and Ān were both captured by Wáng Màidé;
Màidé had previously stationed troops at Qīngní,
so the two generals were intercepted and captured.
He was also captured by the Xià troops.
Yìzhēn was traveling ahead,
and as dusk fell,
the Xià troops did not pursue relentlessly,
so he managed to escape;
his attendants had all scattered,
and he fled alone into the grass.
Duàn Hóng, the Central Army Advisor, rode alone in search of him,
calling out along the way,
Yìzhēn recognized his voice,
came out to meet him,
and said:
"Are you not Advisor Duàn?
I am here,
let's go!
People of Jìn often refer to themselves as 'shēn' (this body).
You could cut off my head and take it south,
so that my father will give up hope."
During the Wèi and Jìn periods,
sons referred to their fathers as 'jiāgōng',
and others referred to them as 'zūngōng'.
Wěn,
fú fěn fān.
"We share life and death,
I cannot bear to do that."
So he tied Yìzhēn to his back,
and rode back alone on his horse.
Yìzhēn said to Hóng:
"Today's events,
truly lacked strategy;
but if a man does not experience this,
how can he understand hardship!"
The Xià King Bóbó wanted to persuade Fù Hóngzhī to surrender,
but Hóngzhī refused to yield,
so Bóbó stripped him naked,
and Hóngzhī shouted curses until he died.
Bóbó piled up human heads to make a jīngguàn,
calling it the Skull Platform.
The people of Cháng'ān drove out Zhū Língshí,
so Língshí burned the palaces,
and fled to Tóngguān.
Since Yìzhēn had plundered Cháng'ān extensively before leaving,
the people of Cháng'ān naturally viewed the Jìn people with enmity.
Língshí, following the Duke of Sòng's orders, could have returned with Yìzhēn,
yet he foolishly remained in Cháng'ān waiting to be driven out—
why?
Bóbó held a grand feast for his officers and soldiers,
raised his cup and said to Wáng Màidé:
"Your words from before,
have now come true as predicted,
truly showing flawless strategy.
This cup of wine,
who else but you deserves it!"
He appointed Màidé as Minister of Personnel,
and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Héyáng.
General Wáng Jìngxiān of the Longxiang Army was garrisoned at Cáogōng's Fort,
Cáogōng's Fort was at Tóngguān,
built when Cáo Cāo attacked Hán and Mǎ.
Xiāng,
sī jiāng fān.
Zhū Chāoshí arrived at Púbǎn,
heard where Língshí was,
and went to join him.
Hèlián Chāng attacked Jìngxiān's fort,
cutting off its water supply;
the defenders grew thirsty,
and could not fight.
As the city was about to fall,
Língshí said to Chāoshí:
"If both brothers die in a foreign land,
how will our elderly parents bear it!
You should find a hidden path and escape back,
I will die here,
with no regrets."
Chāoshí held his elder brother and wept, saying:
"Who does not die?
How could I bear to leave you today!"
So he, along with Jìngxiān and the Right Army Advisor Liú Qīnzhī, were captured and sent to Cháng'ān,
where Bóbó killed them;
Qīnzhī's younger brother Xiùzhī mourned and wept, not enjoying feasts for ten years.
Qīnzhī,
was the son of Mùzhī's cousin.
The Duke of Sòng, Yù, heard of the defeat at Qīngní,
but did not know whether Yìzhēn was alive or dead,
and set a date for a northern expedition.
If Yù could have launched another northern expedition,
then upon hearing of the defeat at Qīngní,
he should have sprung into action immediately,
why wait to set a date!
The actions of heroes,
are certainly not something ordinary people can fathom.
"The soldiers are weary and exhausted,
please wait until another year";
he did not listen.
Huì's request to wait until another year,
also shows Yù's so-called understanding of changing circumstances.
Zhèng Xiānzhī's words were different from this.
He believed:
"If the enemy hears that Your Highness is personally leading the expedition,
they will surely concentrate their forces to defend Tóngguān.
If we directly attack it,
I fear it will not be easily captured;
if the imperial carriage halts at Luò,
then it would not be worth troubling Your Majesty's person.
Moreover, although the enemy has gained an advantage,
they dare not press past Shǎn,
still in awe of Your great majesty,
out of consideration for the future.
If we go to Luò and then return,
the enemy will surely speculate further,
perhaps increasing border troubles.
Besides, with the main army far away,
there will be many troubles at home.
Last year's western expedition,
Liú and Zhōng were in dire straits;
referring to the time in the eleventh year when bandits attacked Yětíng.
Guǎngzhōu fell;
referring to when Xú Dàoqī captured Guǎngzhōu.
These are lessons from the past.
Now, with great floods in various provinces,
the people have little food,
and bandits in Sānwú have attacked and captured several counties,
all due to the hardships of conscription and labor.
The gentry and commoners of Jiāngnán,
crane their necks and gaze eagerly
hoping for Your Highness's return,
if they hear of another northern expedition,
not understanding the depth of the strategy,
nor the timeline for departure and return,
I fear that worries about turning back will lie closer to the heart.
If we are concerned that the western enemy will again threaten Hé and Luò,
we should form an alliance with the northern enemy;
if the northern enemy is friendly, then Hénán will be secure,
the northern enemy,
refers to Wèi.
Hǎo,
hū dào fān.
When he received Duàn Hóng's report,
learning that Yìzhēn had escaped,
Yù then stopped,
only climbing the city wall to gaze north,
sighing deeply and shedding tears.
He demoted Yìzhēn to General of Jianwei and Inspector of Sī Province;
appointed Duàn Hóng as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate of the Sòng administration, concurrently serving as Right Guard Commander of the Crown Prince.
Yù appointed Máo Dézǔ, the Grand Administrator of Tiānshuǐ, as Grand Administrator of Hédōng,
replacing Liú Zúnkǎo in defending Púbǎn.
Although Yù knew Dézǔ was good at defense and appointed him,
morale was already shaken,
so it was natural he could not hold firm.
This sets the stage for Dézǔ's later abandonment of Púbǎn.
16. The Xià King Bóbó built an altar at Bàshàng,
ascended the imperial throne,
and changed the era name to Chāngwǔ.
17. The Western Qín King Chìpán toured the east;
in the twelfth month,
he relocated over five thousand households from Shàngguī to Fúhǎn.
The Duke of Liáng, Lǐ Xīn, employed punishments that were excessively severe,
and furthermore was fond of constructing palace buildings.
The Attendant Gentleman of the Household, Zhāng Xiǎn, submitted a memorial,
stating:
"The Liáng region is divided into three parts,
referring to the Lǐ clan, the Jǔqú clan, and the Qǐfú clan.
The foundation for unification
lies in diligently attending to agriculture;
the strategy for winning over distant regions
is none better than being lenient and simple.
Since the beginning of this year,
the forces of yīn and yáng have been disordered,
wind and rain have been contrary and unseasonable;
this is a time when one should reduce the variety of food and remove the musical instruments.
In ancient times,
the Son of Heaven's meals used six sacrificial animals,
namely horse, ox, sheep, dog, pig, and chicken.
The feudal lords used three sacrificial animals for their meals.
'Xuán'
refers to the hanging of musical instruments.
The Son of Heaven had a full set of instruments hung in the palace,
while the feudal lords had a half set.
In times of great famine,
great pestilence,
when heaven and earth send down calamities,
or when the state faces major troubles,
then the variety of food is reduced and music is suspended.
The Gǔliáng Commentary says: When the five grains do not ripen, it is called a heavenly famine.
One grain not ripening is called 'qiàn',
two grains not ripening is called 'jī',
three grains not ripening is called 'jǐn',
four grains not ripening is called 'kāng',
five grains not ripening is called 'dà qīn'.
According to the rites for a 'dà qīn' famine,
the ruler does not eat more than one kind of dish,
towers and pavilions are not plastered,
archery targets are relaxed and courtyard paths are not cleared,
the various officials perform their duties but do not conduct sacrifices,
prayers are made to ghosts and spirits but sacrifices are not offered.
The Báihǔ Tōng states: When one grain does not ripen, quail and partridge are removed from the meals;
when two grains do not ripen, wild duck and goose are removed;
when three grains do not ripen, pheasant and rabbit are removed;
when four grains do not ripen, the number of animals in the parks is reduced;
when five grains do not ripen, the three sacrificial animals are not fully prepared.
Yet now, on the contrary, punishments are multiplied and laws made harsh,
construction and building do not cease;
this is hardly the way to achieve prosperity.
In the past, King Wén of Zhōu rose to power with a territory of only a hundred lǐ,
while the Second Emperor of Qín perished despite possessing the entire realm.
King Wén of Zhōu rose in Qízhōu,
a territory of a hundred lǐ square.
The Second Emperor of Qín succeeded Qín Shǐ Huáng,
in possession of the entire realm,
yet ultimately met destruction.
Success and failure are clearly evident.
Our Great Ancestor, with his divine and sagely bearing,
was upheld by the Western Xià.
To the left, he captured Jiǔquán,
to the right, he opened up the Western Regions.
Lǐ Gǎo's temple name was Great Ancestor.
Being upheld by the Western Xià
is recorded in the 112th scroll, in the fourth year of the Emperor Ān's Lóng'ān era;
the capture of Jiǔquán
is recorded in the fifth year;
the opening of the Western Regions
is also recorded in the fourth year.
Xià is pronounced 'hù yǎ'.
He unified the Liáng region,
matching the achievements of the later Zhāng rulers.
The 'later Zhāng rulers'
refers to Zhāng Guǐ and his sons and grandsons.
Jǔqú Méngxùn,
an outstanding figure among the Hú and Yí tribes,
internally cultivated governmental affairs,
externally treated the worthy and talented with courtesy.
During battles,
he shared the hardships equally with his soldiers;
the common people cherished him,
and were willing to serve him.
I believe Your Highness not only cannot pacify and eliminate Méngxùn,
but should also fear that Méngxùn may become a worry for the altars of soil and grain."
Xīn read it
and was displeased.
